name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in CI with *read-only* mode for one week, then enforce rules. It lets us test how the tool behaves in our workflow without risking bad merges. The trade-off is a short delay before full enforcement, but we avoid breaking changes while proving the value. After the week, we’ll switch to strict mode only if the dry run shows no issues.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower feedback—it’s that dry-run normalizes noise. PR-Agent’s edits sitting unchecked in PRs train teams to ignore its output, making enforcement later feel like an arbitrary rule change. Instead, run a two-week *sample* of enforced edits on a non-critical branch, then expand—this proves both the tool’s value and the team’s tolerance for its noise without polluting main workflows. Settle it by measuring how often PR-Agent’s suggestions are accepted or rejected in each phase.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in enforce mode on a single non-blocking PR per day for two weeks, then expand to all PRs. This tests the tool’s impact without slowing down critical work, proving its value before full adoption.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in enforce mode on a single non-critical PR per day for two weeks, then expand to all PRs. This proves the tool’s real impact without blocking urgent work—we see actual edits, not just noise. The trade-off is accepting a small daily overhead to validate the tool’s value before full rollout. After two weeks, we’ll have concrete data to decide whether to enforce everywhere or adjust the rules.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Start with one non-blocking PR per day under PR-Agent enforce mode for two weeks, then expand to all PRs if the tool proves its value without disrupting critical work.

Result: A tested, low-risk path to full PR-Agent adoption with clear metrics on its impact. Owner: Overhaul.
